reason: All seven value columns are green-onion-fried oils that differ only in the vegetable oil used, with no unfried/raw reference or other processing contrast in the table, so it compares frying media (formulation) rather than reporting a process effect.
foods: green onion (Allium fistulosum L.) stalks fried in soybean, palm, olive, corn, sunflower, camellia and colza oil (fried green onion oils)
treatments: frying: vegetable oil (300 g) heated to 140 °C, green onion stalks (cut into ~1 cm sections) added and fried until the oil reached 165 °C (minimum slightly below 100 °C); stalks separated, oil cooled; procedure repeated twice and oils mixed
methods_quote: Generally, vegetable oil (300 g) was added into the basin and was heated to 140 °C. Green onion stalks were then added to the hot oil and fried until the oil reached the desired final temperature of 165 °C.
